title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(市来誠研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Ichiki Makoto)
keywords: Composite materials 2.Mechanics and fracture of composites 3.Molding and processing 4.SX,GX 5.Regional collaboration
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) Acquire the ability to identify and solve problems to research, develop, design, and manufacture socially useful and high-quality products using the basic knowledge learned in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. (2) Learn what technologies or new mechanisms are needed for that purpose. (3) Learn about the importance of collaboration with society (particularly local communities).
advice: This is the final comprehensive course in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. To realize the educational objectives of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, this course focuses on the following goals: Students will acquire the ability to model phenomena accurately and analyze the models. Students will acquire the ability and the engineering sense to evaluate solutions based on the obtained results. In practice, students should reconfirm their project theme, which was determined in Preparatory Seminar, with the supervisors of the individual laboratories. (The theme should be revised as necessary.) Students are expected to pursue the identification and solution of problems in accordance with the engineering process. Our laboratory focuses on advanced composite materials, primarily carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRP), which are used in many industrial fields as lightweight structural materials. We carry out project activities aimed at advancing technologies of composite materials to reduce the weight and energy consumption of mechanical structures and create highly reliable structures of composites. Through process development and study of the mechanisms of composite materials, we practice a multifaceted approach and cultivate flexible thinking and comprehensive analytical skills that transcend the boundaries of specialty.
books: Textbooks: None specified Reference books: None specified Reserved books: None specified
requiredKnowledge: - Basic knowledge and understanding of mechanical engineering in general, especially Materials mechanics, Materials, Thermodynamics, Mechanical design and drafting, and Numerical analysis. - Basic knowledge of operation of machine tools, as well as the use of hand tools and equipment. - A certain level of PC operation, Microsoft Office, CAD/CAM, programming, etc. - A readiness to properly handle equipment and an awareness of health and safety. - A willingness to take on new academic fields, learn from failure, and strive for improvement.

activityGoals.body: Be able to advance your project in accordance with the engineering design process.
Be able to compile the results correctly into an article and discuss the content through presentations.
Be able to act independently to solve the issues presented separately.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Understand the purpose of your project and the advancement process accurately, and achieve the established annual goal. The process can be reported in the Design Project Activity Support System. (2) Compile and present the intermediate results for the project into the interim report. Complete the final report, present it to the Design Project III Public Presentation Review Board. (3) If necessary, design and manufacture your own experimental devices, and also evaluate the performance of the product. (The numbers in the text correspond to those of the student’s action goals.)
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the purpose of your project theme and the advancement process, and achieve the established annual goal. In addition, the process can be reported in the Design Project Activity Support System. (2) Compile intermediate results for the project into the interim report, and present its content. Complete the final report and present it to the Design Project III Public Presentation Review Board. (3) Design and manufacture your own experimental devices if necessary. (The numbers in the text correspond to those of the student’s action goals.)

lessons.content: April - Course introduction - Understanding of safety and health - Master the operation of equipment - Investigate on Research Topic Selection
May - Research the research topic - Prepare a research plan - Master the operation of equipment - Start the research activities
June - Progress the research activities - Preliminary study on the research topics
July - Progress the research activities - Prepare the midterm presentation
September - Progress the research activities - Modify the research contents and plans
December - Progress the research activities - Prepare for the interim presentation - Draft the project report outline
January - Progress the research activities - Summarize the research results - Write the project report
February - Complete the project report - Present the project outcome - Prepare and organize the handover data
